M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Generate a larger set of options by scaling the test set\nvoid generateOptions(std::vector<OptionInput>& options, const size_t numOptions) {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    options.resize(numOptions);\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n        const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n        options[i] = base;\n        \n        // Add some variation for larger datasets\n        const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n        options[i].spot *= factor;\n        options[i].strike *= factor;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<OptionInput>& options, \n                     const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const int numChecks = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(10), options.size());\n    \n    printf(\"Checking computed option prices:\\n\");\n    for (int i = 0; i < numChecks; ++i) {\n        const double computed = results[i];\n        const double expected = options[i].value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n        \n        printf(\"  Option %d: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %d: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzwM4KrXrCoVdNbyrgtW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs with MPI, OpenMP and CUDA together, always. It builds with no warnings, and I tested it on this machine's four RTX 3090s. The Sum and hash differ from the original in the last few digits; see the correctness note below.\n\n**Changes (only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`):**\n\n- **MPI:** the options are split into contiguous blocks, one per rank. Rank 0 gathers all prices in the original order, so the Kahan sum, min/max, samples, and hash are computed exactly as before.\n- **CUDA:** each option is generated from its index on the device and priced with one thread per option. Only the prices come back to the host.\n- **OpenMP:** each rank has one host thread per GPU it owns, so the GPUs on a node run concurrently. Ranks on a node share the GPUs round-robin.\n- **Output and CLI:** the same options and output format. I added two informational lines, `MPI ranks` and `GPUs in use`, and timing is the slowest rank's pricing time, excluding the gather.\n- **CMake:** the project is `CXX CUDA`, and MPI, OpenMP and CUDA are `find_package(... REQUIRED)`. The `.cpp` is compiled by nvcc, with host flags forwarded via `-Xcompiler`. The default CUDA architectures are 70, 80, 86, 90, and you can override them with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`. The executable name is unchanged, and no files were added.\n\n**Verification:**\n\n- For the same options, results are identical across 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 ranks, including N=0 and N smaller than the rank count. Validation passes.\n- Against the original CPU binary, the prices agree to about 1e-14 relative. The Sum and hash differ because CUDA's `erf`/`exp`/`log` are not bit-identical to glibc. Reproducing the old hash bit-for-bit would need CPU-side pricing, which would conflict with the requirement to use CUDA unconditionally.\n- At N=1e8, the original CPU run took 9138 ms (about 11M options/s). The hybrid build took 133 ms on 1 rank and 94 ms on 4 ranks (about 0.75–1.07B options/s).\n- At the default N=10000, the GPU is underused and the run takes well under a millisecond of pricing.\n\n**Limitations:**\n\n- Gather counts use `int`, so N is capped at `INT_MAX`. The program reports this and exits.\n- I built the test binary by extracting the original source from the transcript log in `output.txt`. The extracted file is the same as the one I had read, but it was not checked against git (the repo isn't under git)."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":952,"cache_read_input_tokens":71856,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":952},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6745a9e2-371d-45a9-9751-ab5f2bdad4b1","uuid":"b36e69c0-be6e-47b0-b06f-d9b140ebc774","timestamp":"2026-10-13T21:22:02.231Z","request_id":"req_011CfzwM42Fwj2XPH5niwNxs"}
